name: California

sales.rateNote: Statewide base rate of 7.25% since January 1, 2017: 6.00% state portion plus 1.25% local (Bradley-Burns) portion levied everywhere. Voter-approved district taxes of 0.10% to 2.00% each are added in most areas.

local.levies: district taxes adopted by cities, counties and special districts (transportation, public safety, general purpose), on top of the statewide 1.25% Bradley-Burns local tax
local.capNote: The combined rate of district taxes in a county may not exceed 2% (R&T Code 7251.1), but specific statutes authorize some jurisdictions to exceed it.

groceries.note: Food products for human consumption are exempt (Regulation 1602, R&T Code 6359); hot prepared food and meals are taxable.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable at the full rate; California has no clothing exemption or sales tax holiday.

sales.holidayNote: California has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: Use tax applies at the same rate (plus district tax where applicable) to items bought without California tax from out-of-state sellers; individuals can report it on their state income tax return, using CDTFA's lookup table if they wish. Vehicles, vessels and aircraft cannot be reported there.

facts.text: The 7.25% base splits into 6.00% for the state and 1.25% for cities and counties; it has been unchanged since January 1, 2017, when it fell from 7.50%.
District taxes range from 0.10% to 2.00% each, and some areas have more than one.
CDTFA publishes a new city and county rate table each quarter; the current table is effective October 1, 2026.
The statewide rate peaked at 8.25% from April 2009 to June 2011.
Use tax on purchases from out-of-state sellers can be paid on the California income tax return.
Use tax also applies to goods bought abroad and brought into California.

property.levied: Local: counties assess and collect; the revenue goes to counties, cities, schools and special districts. The State Board of Equalization oversees assessment practices.

assessment.text: Proposition 13: real property is assessed at its base-year value (purchase price or value at new construction), which may rise by no more than 2% a year; reassessment to market value on change of ownership or new construction. The general tax rate is 1% of taxable value plus voter-approved debt rates.
assessment.capText: Proposition 13: real property is assessed at its base-year value (purchase price or value at new construction), which may rise by no more than 2% a year; reassessment to market value on change of ownership or new construction. The general tax rate is 1% of taxable value plus voter-approved debt rates.

homestead.name: Homeowners' Exemption
homestead.text: The California Constitution reduces the taxable value of a qualifying owner-occupied home by $7,000. The home must be the owner's principal residence on the January 1 lien date.
homestead.applyBy: One-time claim (BOE-266) with the county assessor; file by February 15 for the full exemption that year.

otherRelief.name: Proposition 19 base-year value transfer
otherRelief.text: Homeowners aged 55+, severely disabled or disaster victims can move their taxable value to a replacement home anywhere in California, up to three times.

otherRelief.name: Proposition 19 parent-child exclusion
otherRelief.text: A family home passed to a child avoids reassessment only if it becomes the child's principal residence, and only up to its factored base-year value plus $1 million (adjusted every other February 16).

otherRelief.name: Active solar exclusion
otherRelief.text: New active solar energy systems are not assessed until a change of ownership; the exclusion is scheduled to sunset January 1, 2027.

dueDates.text: Secured tax bills are mailed by November 1 and paid in two installments: the first is due November 1 and delinquent after December 10; the second is due February 1 and delinquent after April 10.

facts.text: Because assessed values rise by at most 2% a year until a sale, long-time owners usually pay much less than recent buyers of similar homes.
The base property tax rate is 1% of taxable value; voter-approved bonds add to it.
BOE example: a family home with a $300,000 factored base-year value and a $1,500,000 market value is excluded up to $1,300,000, so $200,000 is added to the taxable value.
December 10 is the last day to cancel the Homeowners' Exemption without penalty after a home stops being your principal residence.
February 15 is the legal deadline for most property tax exemption claims.

uncertain: No dedicated CDTFA page read stating that clothing is taxable; 'taxed' reflects the absence of any clothing exemption in the pages read.
The current biennially adjusted Prop 19 amount (base $1,000,000, adjusted February 16, 2025) was not read on the BOE page.
